before: Post-training is additional training applied after a broadly trained model exists.
One approach uses demonstrations of desired responses. Another uses feedback comparing candidate responses or behaviors.
A preference says which candidate was judged better under stated criteria. It is not proof that the preferred answer is factually correct.
These approaches can adjust behavior such as following instructions, but they do not guarantee safety or truth in every future case.
Different systems use different combinations of techniques. This overview does not claim a private recipe for a named unreleased model.
after: Post-training is additional training after a model has learned broad patterns.
It can use demonstrations: examples of desired responses. It can also use feedback comparing responses, such as which one follows an instruction better.
A preference records which answer was judged better for a reason. Check factual accuracy separately when facts matter.
Post-training can improve behavior such as following instructions. It does not guarantee truth or safe behavior in every future case. Different models can use different training methods.

after.question: People prefer answer A because it is clearer, but its date is wrong. Does their preference prove it is accurate?
